title: Dreamland years: Ollie Powers, Jimmie Noone and Charlie Cook
summary: Around 1926-27 he worked with Ollie Powers, Jimmie Noone and Charlie Cook at Dreamland and White City.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: It's been so long, you know. And, uh, uh, we worked there, that was back in, well that must have been 20, that was back in 26, I guess, I don't know, 27. And, uh, I worked with, uh, let's see, there's another fella, had a band, yeah, I don't think you've ever heard of him, cause he didn't get very popular.
There was one band, Glover Compton was telling me the other day of Ollie Powers, worked at the Dreamland too, he was the singer and drummer.

Yes, yes, Ollie Powers was singing there when I was there with Leo, uh huh, yeah, Ollie Powers. And, uh, then he started to drumming there with, uh, I think some, uh, shit. Yeah, he, he, he was, he was very good too, very good singer.
That's what they say, good singer. Yeah. He made a record once with Tommy Ladner and Jimmy Noon and all that.

Oh yes, yes, yes. I have that. Yeah, I worked with Jimmy too, worked with Jimmy Noon, well I used to play at dances. After all. Then I used to, I worked with, uh, Charlie Cook, that was over to Dreamland, over. Oh, the Harman's Westside. Yeah, Westside, uh huh.
The Johnny St. Cyr, I think Noon were over there too. That's right, yeah, that's right, that's right.
Then, uh, we went, uh, I worked with him again at, uh, White City.
Oh yes, was Freddy Kepard with you at the, with Cook's band at that time? No, I, uh, no. Or did you take his place? No, I've taken his place. Uh, Freddy was with him.
